promises.quote: The departure lounge changed its practice to ensure that the staff document in the patients electronic record in line with trust practice. Confirmation of this has been detailed within the departments most recent version of the Standard Operating Procedure (SOP). At the inquest you were shown this SOP in draft form but | can update you now to say that it has now been signed off by the Royal London Hospital's Executive Board.
promises.summary: Signed SOP for electronic record documentation

promises.quote: the departure lounge will now complete documentation audits in line with trust practice for clinical areas to provide assurance that this is being completed.

The departure lounge clarified in their SOP that when a patient is discharged via hospital transport the Discharge Lounge staff will confirm with the Patient Transport Service driver the location and agreed destination for the patient. Any discrepancy must be escalated to the ward area for confirmation and Senior Clinical Site Manager if this discrepancy persists.
As an action the Associate Director of Transport has arranged to review the current safeguarding processes in place and this process will be amended according to their findings.

After the initial Serious Incident (SI) investigation we understand there was concern about Mr Boardman choking on fruit, therefore a second investigation was carried out to look at this particular potential incident. It's clear from staff statements that Mr Boardman had taken a bite out of the kiwi fruit before it was removed at 2000. concerns.quote: The absence of a clear computerised record in the RLH departure .l ounge explaining the change of address.
concerns.hazard: lack of clear computerised record of address change

concerns.quote: The lack of a clear safeguard to ensure that a vulnerable patient is discharged to the correct address.
concerns.hazard: lack of safeguard for discharge to correct address

concerns.quote: The failure of RLH transport staff to properly assess the suitability of the venue that a patient is being taken to.
The responsiveness of the care provider commissioned by LBTH to escalate the fact that they had been unable to reach Mr Boardman for his first 3 care visits.
The proper monitoring of patients on RLH ward 14F who have been · assessed as being ''fed at risk". Specifically, why was a vulnerable patient left with unsuitable foods within his reach.
concerns.hazard: inadequate monitoring of fed at risk patients

concerns.quote: The RLH failure to commence CPR when a potential reversible cause for collapse existed that would override the effect of the DNAR order.
concerns.hazard: failure to initiate CPR despite reversible cause

reports.title: Monica Wood: Prevention of future deaths report

concerns.quote: There appears to have been no provision or mechanism to review the fitness of a patient for travel where the transfer from the Royal London Hospital to another hospital had been delayed by a number of days.
concerns.hazard: lack of provision to review fitness for travel

concerns.quote: There appears to have been no mechanism to review the suitability of the chosen transport and crew for a patient whose condition has materially changed from the point of booking to the point of transfer.
concerns.hazard: lack of mechanism to review transport suitability

links.explanation: Both reports highlight a lack of proper assessment of transport suitability for patients. The earlier focuses on venue assessment at discharge, while the later concerns reviewing transport and crew when a patient's condition changes.
